newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light takes stake in Taiwan project.
newsitem.headline: China Light takes stake in Taiwan project.

text.p: A top official with China Light and Power Co Ltd said on Monday the company has exercised its option to take a stake in a power plant project in Taiwan.
"Earnings from this project should come onstream in 2002," Ross Sayers, chief executive and managing director, said at a news conference.
The company exercised its option to take a 30 percent equity in the 1,320 megawatt power plant to be built near Hualian on Taiwan's eastern coast, the company said in a statement.

China Light, faced with slowing growth in electricity demand in Hong Kong, has sought to expand overseas and is currently studying or negotiating projects in China, India, Thailand, and Indonesia, apart from Taiwan.

Beijing in July approved China Light's plan to construct four power plants with a total generating capacity of 3,220 megawatts in northeastern Shandong province but the lack of loan guarantees appears to be holding up plans.
"I believe only one (foreign-invested) power plant project in China in the past four years has been able to get a PRC state bank loan guarantee, said Sayers.
